title: Anuv Jain Says Independent Music Lets Him Wait for Right Bollywood Project
excerpt: The Ludhiana singer-songwriter told IANS he has had Bollywood offers but is 'quite selective,' crediting his independent releases for the financial and audience foundation that lets him choose his first film project carefully.
body:
• Singer-songwriter Anuv Jain told IANS in Mumbai on November 4 that he has had a few offers from Bollywood and is waiting for the right project, describing himself as "quite selective."
  • He credited his independent releases with building the financial and audience foundation that gives him, in his words, the luxury of being more selective.
  • Jain, from Ludhiana in Punjab, sings primarily in Hindi, with songs about love and longing; BBC Newsbeat reported 3.9 million Instagram followers and more than 20 million monthly listeners on Spotify.
  • His tracks Jo Tum Mere Ho and Afsos, with AP Dhillon, both reached number one on the Asian Music Charts, and he spoke as he finished the European leg of his first world tour at a sold-out London Roundhouse show.

Anuv Jain is in no hurry to enter Bollywood. Speaking in Mumbai, the independent singer-songwriter told IANS that despite offers from Bollywood coming his way, he is patiently waiting for the right project, and that his independent music keeps him occupied, inspired and financially secure, The Freedom Press reported on November 4.

"There have been a few offers from Bollywood, and I would really like to wait for the right project to come my way. I'm quite selective," he said, on the possibility of creating original music for films. "It's not out of any disrespect to anybody, but I feel that if I do something, I want to do it right and give it my best."

Who Anuv Jain is

For readers meeting him here first: Jain is a singer-songwriter from Ludhiana in the Punjab region of India who began singing as a teenager, BBC Newsbeat reported in an interview syndicated by The Geneva Times. He sings primarily in Hindi, and his songs, built around emotional storylines about relationships, love and longing, have racked up hundreds of millions of views on YouTube. His accessible style has attracted 3.9 million followers on Instagram and more than 20 million monthly listeners on Spotify, figures BBC Newsbeat cited as he prepared for the final shows of the European leg of his first world tour, including a sold-out performance at London's Roundhouse.

Jain describes independent artists like himself as existing in an "alternate space" to Bollywood, which has traditionally dominated India's music industry with opportunities and significant funding. "We release music ourselves and hope for the best," he told Newsbeat. His results argue the space is bigger than that framing suggests: Jo Tum Mere Ho and Afsos, his track with AP Dhillon, both reached number one on the Asian Music Charts.

Why he can wait

Jain credited his independent journey, rather than any film placement, for the freedom to choose. In the IANS interview he said the music he has released independently has given him both creative and financial room to turn down work that does not fit.

"I've been very fortunate that all the music I've released independently has helped me build a strong foundation for myself, both financially and in terms of my audience. That has also given me the luxury of being a little more selective."

— Anuv Jain, Singer-songwriter

His writing process, as he described it to BBC Newsbeat, is built for that independent audience rather than for a film brief. He imagines how someone listening in a car, going for a run or sitting alone at night would feel hearing a song. "I just try to make a good song and something that I would like to listen to, something my mum, my sister and my wife would like to listen to," he said. "It's not about the numbers," he added, backstage at the Roundhouse.

What he admires, and what he wants next

Asked about the singers he grew up listening to, Jain named Arijit Singh, Atif Aslam, Sonu Nigam, Shaan and Lata Mangeshkar, IANS reported. "Someone like Arijit Singh, who has been such a benchmark for our generation and someone we all look up to. Then there's Atif Aslam sir, whose music, including his work on Coke Studio, has been absolutely amazing. I also have immense admiration for Sonu Nigam sir, Shaan sir and Lata Mangeshkar ma'am," he said.

One collaboration remains on his wishlist: writing for Shreya Ghoshal. "Shreya Ghoshal has such a beautiful and incredible voice. I would genuinely love to have the opportunity to work with her someday and write something for her. I think that would be really special," he said.

For now, the position is unchanged: a Bollywood entry, when it comes, will be on a project he chooses, financed by a career he built without one.
nri_angle: Jain's sold-out London Roundhouse show and more than 20 million monthly Spotify listeners show that diaspora and streaming audiences can now sustain an Indian independent career without a Bollywood launch.
author: Diaspora Desk

items.label: Number One Hits on Asian Music Charts
